Best Invoicing Software for Freelancers

The best invoicing software for a freelancer is the one that gets you paid with the least fuss — and for many that means free. This guide picks by how you work: free-first invoicing, hands-off automation, or one tool for your whole admin, with an honest note on who each is wrong for.

By The GridDojo Team Published August 31, 2026 5 min read

For a freelancer, invoicing is the least glamorous and most important admin you do — it is how you get paid. The good news is that the tools are mature and several excellent ones are free, so the goal is not to find the most powerful option but the one that gets a professional invoice out and money in with the least friction. This guide sorts the leading tools by how you actually work: free-first invoicing, hands-off automation, or one tool that runs your whole freelance back office. For each, you will also see who it is the wrong choice for.

What a freelancer actually needs from invoicing

  • Professional invoices, fast. Clean, branded invoices you can send in a couple of minutes.
  • Getting paid online. Accept card or bank payment so clients can pay from the invoice itself.
  • Recurring and reminders. Auto-send repeat invoices and chase late payers without you nagging.
  • Basic reports. See what is paid, outstanding, and overdue at a glance for tax and cash flow.
  • A price that fits. As a one-person business, a free or low-cost plan is usually all you need.

The best invoicing tools for freelancers

The tools below are the ones that consistently fit freelancers. Descriptions are based on each vendor's current documented plans, not on hands-on testing. Free tiers and pricing change often, so treat any detail as "at the time of writing" and confirm it on the vendor's own pricing page before you commit.

Wave — best free invoicing with accounting

Wave is the standout free option: it offers unlimited invoices and clients at no cost, and pairs invoicing with genuine bookkeeping, so you can track income and expenses in the same place. For a freelancer watching every euro, that combination is hard to beat. You pay only when you accept online payments (a per-transaction fee) or add payroll, so the core invoicing stays free.

Best for: freelancers who want free invoicing and simple accounting together. Skip it if: you need heavy automation, proposals, or contracts built in.

Zoho Invoice — best polished free invoicing

Zoho Invoice is a genuinely free, polished invoicing tool — professional templates, online payments, time tracking, and reminders — and it is a strong choice if invoicing is all you need. Its free plan does carry limits (for example on the number of clients), so it suits freelancers with a focused client list rather than a fast-growing roster.

Best for: a professional, free invoicing tool for a manageable client list. Skip it if: you have many clients and would hit the free-tier caps, or you want full accounting too.

FreshBooks — best when you want billing on autopilot

FreshBooks is a paid tool built around ease and automation: recurring invoices, automatic late-payment reminders, expense tracking, and well-regarded support. If invoicing is eating your time and you would rather it ran itself, FreshBooks is often worth the monthly fee. There is no permanent free plan, only a trial, so it is a paid-from-the-start choice aimed at freelancers with steady income.

Best for: established freelancers who want polish, automation, and support and will pay for it. Skip it if: you are on a tight budget — a free tool covers the basics well.

Bonsai and QuickBooks — the whole back office

Some freelancers want more than invoicing. Bonsai bundles invoicing with contracts, proposals, and a light CRM, so your whole client admin lives in one tool — ideal if you juggle several clients and hate switching apps. QuickBooks leans the other way, toward full accounting and tax, which suits freelancers who need proper books, not just invoices. Both are paid.

Best for: an all-in-one freelance admin tool (Bonsai) or serious accounting and tax (QuickBooks). Skip them if: you only need to send invoices — you are paying for features you will not use.

How to choose

  • Want free invoicing plus basic bookkeeping → Wave.
  • Want polished, free invoicing and a focused client list → Zoho Invoice.
  • Want billing to run itself and will pay for it → FreshBooks.
  • Want contracts and CRM in the same tool → Bonsai.
  • Need full accounting and tax, not just invoices → QuickBooks.
Tip: Start free unless you already know you need automation. Wave or Zoho Invoice will get you paid professionally at zero cost — see the best free invoicing software for all the free options — and you can move up to a paid tool the day invoicing starts eating hours you would rather bill.

Invoicing is one part of running a freelance business; tracking clients and follow-ups is another. Frequently asked questions

What is the best free invoicing software for freelancers?

Wave and Zoho Invoice are the standout free options. Wave offers unlimited invoices and clients plus basic accounting, while Zoho Invoice gives polished, professional invoicing for free with some limits, such as on client numbers. Both let you get paid professionally at no cost.

Do freelancers need paid invoicing software?

Not necessarily. A free tool like Wave or Zoho Invoice covers professional invoicing and online payments well. Paid tools like FreshBooks or Bonsai add automation, contracts, and support that pay off once invoicing takes real time or you want your whole admin in one place.

Can I get paid directly through an invoice?

Yes. Most invoicing tools let you add an online payment option so clients can pay by card or bank transfer straight from the invoice. This usually carries a per-transaction fee, but it gets you paid faster than manual bank transfers.

Is invoicing software the same as accounting software?

Not quite. Invoicing software focuses on billing clients and getting paid; accounting software adds full bookkeeping, expenses, and tax. Some tools blur the line — Wave includes basic accounting, and QuickBooks is accounting-first — so pick based on whether you need books or just invoices.
